readers.name: autophagy
requirements: A recycling station can hold a large pile because more material arrives or because processing has slowed. The pile is an amount; material processed over time is a rate. Neither alone tells you whether the city depends on that station.

Yamamoto and colleagues found that the cargo receptor NBR1 helped direct MHC-I proteins to lysosomes through an autophagy-dependent route in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma models. This lowered the amount of MHC-I at the cell surface, where it displays antigens to CD8 T cells. In mouse experiments, reducing MHC-I or depleting CD8 T cells reversed tumour control after genetic autophagy inhibition. Chloroquine increased surface MHC-I but, alone, did not significantly reduce tumour weight in the reported experiment; its effects on lysosomes are broad. These model results do not establish that every KRAS-driven cancer depends on autophagy or that blocking it benefits patients.

readers.name: mechanics-apoptosis-bcl2
requirements: A dam (the mitochondrial membrane) held by guards (BCL-2, MCL-1, BCL-XL) against demolition crews (BAX, BAK). Cancer hires extra guards; venetoclax fires the BCL-2 guards. Immune killing uses the same dam from the outside.
Cancer cells can change how they manage damage, recycling and death.

readers.name: mechanics-dna-repair-synthetic-lethality
requirements: Double-strand breaks (HR versus end joining), copying errors (mismatch repair), and single damaged letters (base excision, PARP) each have their crew. Tumours that lost one crew survive on the others, and that dependence is the first widely successful way to drug a lost gene.
